record_notes.DCP-LETT-2416: Six body blocks, all five notes and bibliography read. February 20 [1859]. Enclosed autograph list is not reproduced. Ghost stories, honeysuckle becoming oak and new railway species are playful social remarks, not asserted scientific results. The Moor Park fortnight is completed and Etty reported recovered; Lady Drysdale station story remains reported. No surviving incoming Butler prompt identified.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2489: Four blocks, three notes and bibliography read. September 11 [1859]. Missing address inquiry and response place Butler in Scotland. Book nearly finished with forecast completion at month end; proposed October Ilkley stay, family attendance and house rental remain undecided. Later October family arrival and Butler visit are editorial retrospective facts, not current knowledge. No preserved prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2538: Complete three-block copy, five notes and bibliography read. After November 21, 1859 has open TEI upper bound 1882; held across publication boundary. Answers missing Caroline questions. Domestic dog differences attributed partly to multiple wild sources, while those wild species share earlier ancestors: distinct claims. Lyell having been bothered by the same point does not uniquely identify a particular earlier Lyell letter. Athenaeum review already read and judged unfair; conversion of four or five judges is a hope. Future Jos criticism not yet received.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2420: Three blocks, four notes, bibliography and actual billiard-frame figure read. February 24 [1859]. William forwarding address in P1 is authorial routing prose, not a removable header. Installers left London at 2 AM and completed table by dinner. Eight legs, four slate slabs and staged levelling remain separate counts. Actual drawing is a rectangular three-by-three grid with eight perimeter black dots at corners and mid-sides and a small interior ring; nine grid cells are not nine legs. No letter or numeral labels. Price £53 s18.0 is supported as £53 18s by accounting apparatus; raw stictched remains a transcription-review item. Supplier naming correction belongs to apparatus. No incoming prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2498A: Eleven retained blocks, ten notes and bibliography read. October 22 OR October 29, 1859 are discrete alternatives. Hornet combs requested in three or four weeks, not already dispatched or received. P2-6 C. Darwin/care of G. Snow/Nags Head/Southwark/London is the authorial shipping instruction and must survive header removal. P7 ends with at least one page missing after violent; no reconstruction. Supplied [Moor] and missing-page notice distinguished from authorial text. Family is already present; four or five further weeks and uncertain invitation plans are forecasts. P11 sheet-order explanation is authorial.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2380: Five blocks, eight notes and bibliography read. December 12, 1858 is within cutoff. Missing October 28 note arrived about a week earlier, pigeon treatise a few days subsequently; these are separate approximate receipt events. Treatise has been read enough to interest and amuse, but full translation is not transcribed here. Kaseen fowls already received, currently with Tegetmeier; British Museum deposit prospective, and later partial 1867 deposit is not current. Elliot joining Linnean Society prospective. Horse and ass stripe requests not findings; unspecified northwest India information does not uniquely establish a Poole knowledge edge. Apparatus January26 reference differs from actual January23 date of 1824.

Father flood, acquired instincts and disease questions are historical enquiries, not demonstrated mechanisms. Richardson Thursday visit and grant prospective. record_notes.DCP-LETT-1824: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Darwin to Walter Elliot, January 23, 1856. Six blocks, six footnotes, full metadata and bibliography read. Oral Glasgow meeting distinct from request for tiger measurements, eastern translations and long-bred native domestic bird skins. Adult/old specimens and bones, poultry sexes, native names and reimbursement requested; not European recent introductions. Ayin Akbaree translation can be consulted, not already read. Tiger-table verso dated June10 and later judgment not current January data; table itself unavailable here. Later payments not January receipt. P6 address excluded from eventual content; inconsistent translation bibliography not silently harmonized.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2003F: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. George to Darwin, Friday supplied November 28, 1856 from the return-to-school diary. Full sixteen blocks, six footnotes, separate scholarly aside and bibliography read. School illness, confinement, stolen sweets and paint-supply storage requests are George voice; child instructions are source content. Novel reading and knucklebone supposition are not Darwin knowledge or verified anatomy. Separate quill-pen aside is authorial but excluded by projection, requiring later content-policy review. F does not mean missing body. Repeated now now and to put to put are not automatically transcription errors. Missing Darwin/Pritchard communications not reconstructed.

visual_readings.visual_observation: Root viewed actual preserved image: rectangular three-by-three grid, eight dark perimeter dots at corners and mid-sides, and a small interior ring. No letter or numeral labels. The eight legs stated in prose are not a count of the nine rectangular cells.

reading_method: Root independently read complete surviving new source bodies, metadata constraints, exclusions, footnotes, scholarly sections and bibliography. Actual special markup and figures inspected where present. Reused explicit accepted primary readings only after matching source and accepted evidence hashes. Historical decisions and notes are handwritten; validation packages evidence rather than adjudicating it.
